address: LAS Rental Car Center, 7135 Gilespie St, Las Vegas, NV 89119
highway: AA 2356 JFK → LAS · Pick-up 11:30 AM
note: Land LAS at 10:56 AM on American Airlines AA 2356 from JFK. Pick up confirmed Midsize SUV (Nissan Rogue or similar) at 11:30 AM ($466.67 total, unlimited miles, CDW + SLP + Roadside PLUS included).
eat: Hydrate and grab an espresso after landing before loading the SUV.
see: Verify flat-folding rear seats (raise Nissan Rogue Divide-N-Hide floor panel for a dead-flat sleeping deck).

address: Walmart Supercenter (6005 S Eastern Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89119) & REI Henderson (2220 Village Walk Dr, Henderson, NV 89052)
highway: I-215 E · S Eastern Ave
note: 60-min camp gear & grocery provisioning stop (12:00–1:15 PM). Pick up 0°F–15°F sleeping bag, R>=4.5 pad, camp stove + fuel canister, 2.5-gal water jug, Reflectix, and beach towel.
eat: Mothership Coffee Roasters (2708 N Green Valley Pkwy, Henderson) + fresh wraps, fruit, and electrolyte water.
see: One-stop desert & canyon provisioning 8 minutes east of the rental car center.

address: Fire Wave & Seven Wonders Trailhead (Parking Lot #3), White Domes Rd, Moapa Valley, NV 89040
highway: I-15 N · NV-169 E (Exit 75)
note: $15 NV out-of-state entry fee. Hike the 1.8 mi (3.0 km) Fire Wave & Seven Wonders Loop (3:00–4:35 PM) across pink-and-orange Aztec sandstone swirls and through Pastel (Pink) Canyon at golden hour.
eat: 1.5L electrolyte water + trail fruit and bars before heading up White Domes Road.
see: Mouse's Tank Road scenic corridor, Rainbow Vista, Fire Wave striated sandstone, and Pink Canyon slot.

address: La Quinta Inn & Suites by Wyndham La Verkin - Gateway to Zion, 101 E 500 N, La Verkin, UT 84745
highway: I-15 N (Virgin River Gorge) · UT-9 E
note: BOOKED Night 1 Hotel: La Quinta Inn & Suites La Verkin (25 mins from Zion South Gate). Lose 1 hour crossing NV -> UT (PST to MST). Soak post-marathon legs in the hot tub. (Alt camp: Watchman or Hurricane Cliffs BLM).
eat: Stage Coach Grille (99 N State St, La Verkin) or Casa Tequilana (Hurricane).
see: Towering limestone walls of the Virgin River Gorge along I-15.

address: The Grotto / Temple of Sinawava, Zion Canyon Scenic Drive, Springdale, UT 84767
highway: UT-9 E · Zion Canyon Scenic Drive
note: Buy $80 America the Beautiful Pass at Zion South Gate. In Nov, drive your own SUV directly up Zion Canyon Scenic Drive! Hike Option 1: Scout Lookout / Angels Landing (8.7 km), Option 2: Extended West Rim Trail (11.5 km), or Option 3: Deep Narrows via Zion Outfitter.
eat: 7:00 AM coffee & breakfast burrito at River Rock Roasting Co (La Verkin); 3:00 PM recovery snack at Sol Foods or Deep Creek Coffee in Springdale.
see: 2,000-ft Navajo sandstone cliffs, Scout Lookout views over the Big Bend, and the Virgin River narrows.

address: Canyon Overlook Trailhead (East Portal of Zion-Mt. Carmel Tunnel), UT-9, Springdale, UT
highway: UT-9 E · Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway
note: Drive the historic 1.1-mile 1930 tunnel at 3:45 PM, park at the East Portal, and hike the 1.0 mi (1.6 km) Canyon Overlook Trail for sunset (5:27 PM MST) over Pine Creek slot and West Temple.
eat: Thermos tea & trail mix on the East Temple sandstone ledges.
see: Pine Creek Canyon abyss, switchbacks below, and West Temple glowing crimson at sunset.

address: Best Western East Zion Thunderbird Lodge, US-89 & UT-9, Mt. Carmel Junction, UT 84755
highway: UT-9 E · US-89
note: Sleep on the East Zion plateau so you don't backtrack tomorrow. Options: Best Western Thunderbird Lodge (Mt. Carmel Jct), Canyons Boutique Hotel (Kanab), Zion Ponderosa Cowboy Cabin, or East Zion BLM camp.
eat: Cordwood at Zion Mountain Ranch (farm-to-table bison/trout), Thunderbird Restaurant ('Ho-Made' pies), or Peekaboo Canyon Wood Fired Kitchen (Kanab).
see: Checkerboard Mesa on the drive out of East Zion and star-filled plateau skies.

address: Red Canyon Visitor Center & Arch Tunnels, UT-12, Panguitch, UT 84759
highway: US-89 N · Scenic Byway UT-12 E
note: Drive through the two hand-carved red-rock highway arches on UT-12, then stop at Ruby's Inn General Store for warm layers, fuel, and trail provisions.
eat: Roadside espresso + hot lunch provisions from Ruby's Inn General Store.
see: Vibrant crimson Claron limestone hoodoos and the iconic Red Canyon arch tunnels.

address: Sunset Point / Inspiration Point & Ruby's Inn, UT-63, Bryce Canyon City, UT 84764
highway: UT-12 E · UT-63 S
note: FREE entry w/ $80 Pass. Hike the Figure-8 Combination Loop (Wall Street + Navajo Loop + Queens Garden + Peekaboo Loop, 10.3 km) or Fairyland Loop (12.9 km). Watch sunset at Inspiration Point (5:23 PM MST). Night temp drops to -6°C (21°F). Sleep: Ruby's Inn, Bryce Pioneer Village (Tropic), North Campground, or Dixie NF FR-117.
eat: i.d.k. Barbecue (Tropic, UT — local smoked brisket & ribs) or Valhalla Pizzeria & Coffee Shop at Bryce Canyon Lodge.
see: Thousands of glowing orange hoodoo spires, Thor's Hammer, Wall Street slot, and 8,100-ft stargazing.

address: Kanab Creek Bakery, 238 E 300 S, Kanab, UT 84741
highway: UT-12 W · US-89 S
note: After catching the 7:04 AM sunrise over Bryce Point, descend US-89 S to Kanab for freshly baked sourdough, croissants, espresso, and packed trail sandwiches.
eat: Kanab Creek Bakery — scratch sourdough, savory quiche, French pastries, and trail baguettes.
see: Dawn light igniting the Bryce amphitheater before dropping 3,000 ft down the Grand Staircase.

address: Wire Pass Trailhead, House Rock Valley Rd, Kanab, UT 84741
highway: US-89 E · House Rock Valley Rd (BLM 1065)
note: Midday unguided slot canyon hike! Option 1: Wire Pass into Buckskin Gulch ($6 permit, 9–13 km round-trip into the longest/deepest slot canyon in the Southwest). Option 2 (if muddy): Willis Creek Narrows + Toadstool Hoodoos (2.4 km right off US-89).
eat: Packed Kanab Creek Bakery sandwich & trail snacks at the Wire Pass / Buckskin confluence alcove.
see: 200-ft sculpted Navajo sandstone narrows, petroglyph panel at the confluence, and balanced Toadstool boulders.

city: Glen Canyon Dam & Horseshoe Bend Overlook
address: Horseshoe Bend Overlook, US-89 Milepost 545, Page, AZ 86040
highway: US-89 S across Glen Canyon Bridge
note: Stop at Glen Canyon Dam Overlook (3:45 PM, free w/ pass), then walk the 1.5 mi (2.4 km) round-trip trail to Horseshoe Bend Overlook ($10 Page parking) for sunset (5:22 PM MST) 1,000 ft above the Colorado River.
eat: Post-sunset dinner in Page: The BirdHouse (crispy fried chicken & honey butter biscuits) or El Tapatio.
see: 270-degree gooseneck bend of the emerald Colorado River framed by sheer 1,000-ft sandstone cliffs.

address: Lone Rock Beach Campground (Lake Powell) or Hyatt Place Page Lake Powell, 1126 N Navajo Dr, Page, AZ 86040
highway: US-89 · Lake Powell Blvd
note: Sleep on the sand right at the water's edge at Lone Rock Beach ($14 camp fee; $30 Glen Canyon entry waived by $80 pass), Wahweap Campground, or at Hyatt Place / Country Inn & Suites in Page.
eat: Campfire tea under the stars on Lake Powell shore or local craft draft at Grand Canyon Brewing (Page).
see: Lone Rock monolith rising directly out of Lake Powell under desert starlight.

address: Lower Antelope Canyon (Ken's / Dixie's Tours) or Upper Antelope Canyon, Page, AZ 86040
highway: AZ-98 E · Antelope Point Rd
note: 9:15 AM Guided Navajo Slot Canyon Tour (check in 8:30 AM). Lower Antelope (Ken's or Dixie's Tours) descends staircases through corkscrewing V-shaped sandstone corridors; Upper Antelope is a flat walk-in.
eat: Morning espresso & breakfast sandwich at LP Espresso or Canyon Crepes Cafe in Page.
see: World-famous swirling orange-and-violet Navajo sandstone cathedral walls and sculpted light beams.

address: Forrest Gump Point, US-163 Milepost 13, Mexican Hat, UT 84531
highway: AZ-98 E · US-160 E · US-163 N
note: Iconic straight-arrow highway viewpoint looking south into the Monument Valley buttes. Pull completely onto the paved shoulder turnout for photos.
eat: Roadside snack and hydration break before entering Navajo Tribal Park.
see: The classic telephoto road panorama leading straight into the towering red stone mittens and mesas.

address: The View Hotel & Wildcat Trailhead, Indn Route 42, Oljato-Monument Valley, AZ 84536
highway: US-163 · Monument Valley Rd
note: $8 Tribal Park entry. Hike the unguided 5.4 mi (8.7 km) Wildcat Trail right around the base of West Mitten Butte (1:15–3:30 PM), drive the 17-Mile Valley Floor Loop (John Ford's Point, Artist's Point, North Window), and watch sunset over the Mittens (5:16 PM MST). Sleep: The View Hotel / Cabins / Campground or Goulding's Lodge.
eat: Navajo Taco on frybread or green chile stew at The View Restaurant or Goulding's Stagecoach Dining Room.
see: West Mitten, East Mitten, and Merrick Butte glowing deep crimson at sunset and sunrise right outside your door.

address: Cameron Trading Post, 466 US-89, Cameron, AZ 86020
highway: US-160 W · US-89 S
note: Watch the 6:52 AM sunrise over the Monument Valley Mittens, then drive 1h 45m south to historic 1916 Cameron Trading Post at the Little Colorado River Gorge. Top off fuel here before entering the park.
eat: Historic dining room brunch (Navajo Taco or huevos rancheros) + browse authentic Native American basketry & rugs.
see: 1911 suspension bridge spanning the Little Colorado River Gorge.

city: Desert View Watchtower & East Rim Drive
address: Desert View Watchtower, AZ-64 (Desert View Dr), Grand Canyon NP, AZ
highway: AZ-64 W · Grand Canyon East Entrance
note: FREE entry w/ $80 Pass. Enter via the dramatic East Entrance along Desert View Drive (25 mi). Stop at Mary Colter's 1932 stone Watchtower, Lipan Point (best view of the Colorado River & Unkar Delta), and Moran Point.
eat: Trail snacks & espresso before heading to the South Kaibab shuttle.
see: 70-ft stone Watchtower overlooking the widest eastern sweep of the Grand Canyon and the Painted Desert.

city: Grand Canyon South Rim (South Kaibab Trail)
address: South Kaibab Trailhead & Mather Campground, Grand Canyon Village, AZ 86023
highway: AZ-64 W · South Rim Village
note: Hike below the rim on the exposed ridge of the South Kaibab Trail: Option 1: Ooh Aah Point & Cedar Ridge (3.0 mi / 5.5 km, 1,140 ft vertical), Option 2: Skeleton Point (6.0 mi / 9.7 km, 2,040 ft vertical), or Option 3: Paved Rim Trail to Hopi Point. Sunset at Hopi or Yavapai Point (5:26 PM MST). Sleep: Mather Campground ($18), Yavapai Lodge, or Kaibab NF FR-302 free camp.
eat: El Tovar Lounge / Harvey House Cafe at Bright Angel Lodge or hot camp dinner at Mather.
see: 360-degree inner-canyon panoramas from Cedar Ridge and a 1-billion-year geological abyss glowing violet at dusk.

address: Macy's European Coffeehouse & Bakery, 14 S Beaver St, Flagstaff, AZ 86001
highway: AZ-64 S · US-180 E
note: Scenic pine-forest drive past the 12,633-ft San Francisco Peaks into historic downtown Flagstaff (7,000 ft) for Arizona's best independent coffeehouse.
eat: Macy's Special (house mocha w/ real whipped cream) + fresh vegetarian breakfast burrito or waffle.
see: Historic Route 66 brick storefronts and ponderosa pine mountain air.

address: Oak Creek Vista Overlook, N State Route 89A, Sedona, AZ 86336
highway: AZ-89A S · Oak Creek Canyon Switchbacks
note: Stop at Oak Creek Vista Overlook at the rim of the Mogollon Rim, then descend 2,500 ft down hairpin switchbacks under sycamore canopy alongside rushing Oak Creek.
eat: Fresh apple cider or fruit from the Native American artisan stands at Oak Creek Vista.
see: Vertical white-and-crimson canyon walls plunging into lush riparian forest.

address: Cathedral Rock & Dry Creek Vista, Sedona, AZ 86336
highway: AZ-89A · AZ-179 (Red Rock Scenic Byway)
note: Red Rock Pass FREE w/ $80 America the Beautiful Pass; use free weekend Sedona Shuttle to trailheads! Afternoon hike: Option 1: Devil's Bridge (6.8 km), Option 2: Soldier Pass Cave & Seven Sacred Pools (7.2 km), or Option 3: Boynton Canyon (10.0 km). At 4:00 PM, scramble up Cathedral Rock Trail (2.4 km) for 5:27 PM MST sunset. Sleep: Sedona boutique hotel or FR 525 Loy Butte BLM camp.
eat: Lunch at Indian Gardens Cafe & Market (Oak Creek); dinner at The Hudson, Elote Cafe, or Tortas de Fuego.
see: Natural sandstone arch at Devil's Bridge and the fiery orange spires of Cathedral Rock at sunset.

city: Joshua Tree National Park (Barker Dam Loop)
address: Barker Dam Trailhead, Park Blvd, Joshua Tree National Park, CA 92284
highway: I-17 S · I-10 W · Park Blvd
note: Gain 1 extra hour crossing AZ -> CA (MST to PST)! Optional 60-min Mojave leg-flush stop on the flat 1.1 mi (1.8 km) Barker Dam Loop (FREE entry w/ $80 Pass), or stay straight on I-10 W to reach the ocean 90 mins earlier.
eat: 6:30 AM pour-over at FreeForm Coffee Roasters (Sedona); midday date shake & fish tacos in Indio/Palm Springs.
see: Surreal monzogranite boulder wonderland, desert bighorn habitat, and thousands of twisted Joshua trees.

city: Laguna Beach (1,000 Steps Beach & Heisler Park)
address: Heisler Park & 1,000 Steps Beach (9th Ave & Coast Hwy), Laguna Beach, CA 92651
highway: I-10 W · CA-91 W · CA-133 S to Coast Hwy (CA-1)
note: OCEAN NIGHT #1! Arrive Laguna Beach 1:30–2:30 PM. Take your first Pacific Ocean swim (18°C / 64°F water, 22°C sunny air) at 1,000 Steps Beach sea caves or Main Beach coves, walk to Victoria Beach's 1926 Pirate Tower, and stroll Heisler Park tide pools at sunset (4:52 PM PST). Sleep: Laguna Beach House / Art Hotel or Crystal Cove Moro Campground.
eat: Banzai Bowls (acai bowl after swim) + sunset dinner overlooking the surf at The Cliff Restaurant, Nick's Laguna Beach, or La Sirena Grill.
see: Turquoise coves, sea caves, tide pools, and the Pacific sun sinking behind Catalina Island.

address: Crystal Cove Historic District & Reef Point, 8471 N Coast Hwy, Laguna Beach, CA 92651
highway: Pacific Coast Hwy (CA-1 N) · 10 mins north of Laguna
note: Morning coffee at Jedidiah Coffee (Laguna). Hike the 3.0 mi (5.0 km) Reef Point & Pelican Point Bluff-to-Beach Loop and take a refreshing morning ocean swim #2 in the protected marine preserve alongside 1930s vintage beach cottages.
eat: Brunch right on the sand at The Beachcomber at Crystal Cove + date shake at Ruby's Shake Shack on the cliff.
see: 3.2 miles of untouched golden sand, Pelican Point tide pools, and dolphins cruising just beyond the breakers.

address: Venice Canals Historic District & Windward Plaza, Venice, CA 90291
highway: CA-73 N · I-405 N · CA-90 W
note: Stroll the peaceful Venice Canals walkways, watch skaters drop into the beachfront Venice Skatepark & Muscle Beach, then rent a cruiser bike and ride the 6.2 mi (10 km) round-trip Marvin Braude Oceanfront Trail ('The Strand') to Santa Monica Pier at golden hour.
eat: Coffee at Menotti's Coffee Stop (Windward Ave) or Intelligentsia (Abbot Kinney Blvd).
see: 1905 Venice canal bridges, palm-lined oceanfront boardwalk, and golden-hour views up the Santa Monica Bay.

address: Santa Monica Pier & Sea Blue Hotel, 1670 Ocean Ave, Santa Monica, CA 90401
highway: Ocean Ave · Pacific Coast Hwy (CA-1)
note: OCEAN NIGHTS #2 & #3! Watch sunset at the end of the Santa Monica Pier (Route 66 End of the Trail sign, 4:53 PM PST). Base here for two consecutive nights (Tue + Wed) so there is zero hotel packing tomorrow morning. (Alt camp: Leo Carrillo or Point Mugu Thornhill Broome beachfront).
eat: Dinner at Gjelina (Abbot Kinney Blvd), The Misfit Bar, or the iconic Godmother sandwich at Bay Cities Italian Deli.
see: Pacific Park Ferris wheel lights reflecting on the low-tide ocean mirror at dusk.

city: Point Dume Nature Preserve & Pirates Cove
address: Point Dume State Beach & Nature Preserve, Cliffside Dr & Birdview Ave, Malibu, CA 90265
highway: Pacific Coast Hwy (CA-1 N) · 21 mi north of Santa Monica
note: Morning espresso at Caffe Luxxe (Montana Ave) or Dogtown Coffee, then cruise PCH along the Malibu surf. Hike the 1.5 mi (2.4 km) Point Dume Cove Trail over the basalt headlands and climb down the wooden stairs into sheltered Pirates Cove for a morning Pacific swim.
eat: Morning pastry & espresso before driving PCH; bring water & towel down the cove stairs.
see: 360-degree views of Zuma Beach, the Santa Monica Mountains, Catalina Island, and harbor seals in the kelp beds.

address: El Matador State Beach, 32350 Pacific Coast Hwy, Malibu, CA 90265
highway: PCH (CA-1 N) · 4 mi north of Point Dume
note: Descend the dramatic bluff stairs to Malibu's most cinematic pocket beach. Walk through hollowed-out sea caves, sandstone arches, and towering sea stacks, and take one last Pacific plunge.
eat: Hydrate after the beach stairs — big oceanfront seafood feast is next.
see: Wave-carved sea caves, keyhole rock arches, and emerald breakers crashing against golden cliffs.

city: Malibu Seafood Fresh Fish Market & Patio Cafe
address: Malibu Seafood, 25653 Pacific Coast Hwy, Malibu, CA 90265
highway: PCH (CA-1 S)
note: Iconic fishermen-owned Malibu institution sitting directly across PCH from Dan Blocker Beach. Eat outdoors on the terraced ocean-view patio.
eat: Grilled wild Pacific salmon or halibut, clam chowder in sourdough, fish tacos, or classic fish & chips.
see: Unobstructed panoramic views across the sparkling Pacific while eating lunch in the sun.

address: Griffith Observatory, 2800 E Observatory Rd, Los Angeles, CA 90027
highway: I-10 E · I-5 N · Los Feliz Blvd
note: 3:15 PM: Hike the 3.0 mi (4.8 km) Mount Hollywood Trail from the Observatory lawn to the summit for 360° golden-hour views of the Hollywood Sign, Downtown LA skyline, and the Pacific Ocean at sunset (4:52 PM PST). Return to Santa Monica afterward to pack your checked bag.
eat: Celebratory final-night dinner back in Santa Monica / Venice: Forma Restaurant & Cheese Bar, Cassia, or Felix Trattoria.
see: The Hollywood Sign, Art Deco Observatory domes, and the entire Los Angeles basin lighting up from the mountains to the sea.

address: Palisades Park (Ocean Ave, Santa Monica) & Fuel Stop (Aviation Blvd & Century Blvd, Los Angeles, CA)
highway: Ocean Ave · Lincoln Blvd (CA-1 S) · Century Blvd
note: 7:30–9:30 AM final morning walk & coffee along the palm-lined Palisades Park ocean bluffs. Check out by 10:15 AM. Top off fuel tank to 100% full near Aviation Blvd / Century Blvd at 11:00 AM.
eat: Final California breakfast burrito & flat white at Huckleberry Bakery & Cafe (1014 Wilshire Blvd) or Primo Passo Coffee.
see: Morning surfers at the pier and one last deep breath of salt air before heading to LAX.

city: LAX Rental Return & Terminal B (TBIT) — Wheels Up
address: Enterprise/National Return (5251 W 98th St, Los Angeles, CA 90045) & LAX Terminal B (TBIT)
highway: Aviation Blvd · W 98th St · LAX Terminal B
note: Return Midsize SUV at 5251 W 98th St by 11:30 AM sharp (exact 10.0-day $466.67 clock). Shuttle to LAX Terminal B (TBIT) by 12:00 PM. Board 15:00 Lufthansa LH 457 -> FRA (Seat 29A) -> LH 1480 -> EVN (Booking 9Y6YC9).
eat: Pre-flight meal in Tom Bradley International Terminal Great Hall before boarding at 14:15.
see: Takeoff west over the Pacific beaches before banking northeast over the Mojave and Southwest canyons you just conquered.
